question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in per-message timestamps to the core TUI, and should the control be persistent config, an in-session toggle, or both?
rationale: The source-visible gap is clear, but choosing a durable TUI UX/config contract is product direction that automation should not settle while open implementation candidates already exist.

options.title: Approve opt-in TUI timestamps
options.body: Allow a narrow implementation that keeps timestamps disabled by default, uses real message timestamps across live streaming and history replay, and includes PTY-visible proof.

options.title: Prefer session-only toggle
options.body: Avoid expanding persisted config and accept only an in-session TUI control if maintainers want the lighter UX surface.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Keep the TUI visually minimal and close or defer this request in favor of logs or external terminal tooling for timing context.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in TUI timestamps
recommendation.body: Allow a narrow implementation that keeps timestamps disabled by default, uses real message timestamps across live streaming and history replay, and includes PTY-visible proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current local history signal on the TUI lifecycle paths and is the best available owner for the UX/config direction choice.
